neet_che_u06_t14_1.working: A buffer needs a weak acid plus its conjugate base. CH3COOH with CH3COONa is the only such pair; the others pair a strong acid or strong base with a salt.

neet_che_u06_t14_3.working: HCl converts 0.1 mol NH4OH to NH4Cl, leaving 0.2 mol NH4OH and 0.1 mol NH4Cl in 1 L. pOH = pKb + log([salt]/[base]) = 4.74 + log(0.1/0.2) = 4.74 − 0.30 = 4.44. pH = 14 − 4.44 = 9.56.

neet_che_u06_t14_4.working: Dilution lowers salt and acid concentrations by the same factor, so their ratio and the pH stay essentially unchanged. A is true. R is false because the ratio does not increase.

neet_che_u06_t14_5.working: Buffer capacity is greatest when [salt] = [acid], i.e. pH = pKa, so I is correct. A ratio of 100 does give pH 6.74, but that lies outside the effective range pKa ± 1, so II is incorrect.
